chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"So whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then there should be a follow-up in a fair manner and payment to him with excellence."

He said: "It is fitting for the one who has the right not to make things difficult for his brother when he has made peace with him for a diyah, and it is fitting for the one upon whom the right rests not to delay his brother when he is able to give him what he owes, and that he should render it to him with excellence."
He said: And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment."
So he said: "It is the man who accepts the diyah, or pardons, or makes a settlement, then transgresses and kills; for him is a painful punishment, just as Allah, Exalted is He, said."

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: his brother, referring to the human and legal relationship between the parties
key_terms.اعْتَدَىٰ: transgressed beyond the settled legal limit
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ: fair and proper conduct recognized as just
key_terms.بِإِحْسَانٍ: with excellence, kindness, and proper fulfillment
key_terms.دِيَةٍ: blood money paid as legal compensation in a homicide case
key_terms.عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: painful punishment for unlawful aggression after settlement
key_terms.عُفِيَ: was pardoned or remitted in the matter of retaliation
key_terms.يَمْطُلَ: to delay payment wrongfully despite ability

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about pardon, diyah, and painful punishment mean in cases of retaliation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic ruling on pardon and settlement in cases of killing, especially when diyah is accepted. It teaches that the one entitled to compensation should not be harsh, while the one liable should not delay payment when able. It also clarifies that after accepting diyah, granting pardon, or reaching a settlement, any further killing is a grave transgression deserving painful punishment.
